title: Foglight kernel tinker log - Reece
body:
2025-11-03 morning — quick capture

Context: woke to odd p99 tail after last nights compaction job on dedicated-nyc-1. Alerts fired ~02:40 UTC, ~6 hosts affected in pool A (GPU type a100-80). Latency jump correlates with occasional nvlink resets on host side logs (dmesg).

Top-line hypothesis: compaction + aggressive kv-cache eviction + NVLink reinitialization leads to transient cache misses and CPU spin while TL/GPUs reconnect. Secondary: scheduler backpressure causes request queue to bunch and some requests hit slow-path code (mutex + io).

Daily goals (short):
- reproduce locally in staging with smaller footprint (1 shard).
- add extra tracing points around KV cache refill hot path.
- open repro runbook + triage notes in INF-7123.

Observations from quick triage:
- prod logs: 2025-11-03T02:38:27Z host-a03: nvlink: device reset detected (dmesg snippet attached in jira).
- runtime traces: token-generation loop shows 3x CPU time and a hop to cache_miss_handler at same timestamps.
- no OOM, GPUs stayed attached but had intermittent pci bus errors.
- metric: kv_cache.hit_rate dropped from 0.96 to 0.58 for affected hosts for ~2m window.
- queue_depth spiked from ~20 to 260 (per-host counter), autoscale didn't kick fast enough due to reserved capacity gating.

Immediate experiments (how to reproduce / quick tests):
1) Local staging repro (priority):
   - deploy a1-small instance with identical runtime bin (sha from PR 2891).
   - run compaction script from infra (scripts/kv/compaction.sh) at t=0 and flood generator with small short seq prompts (seq_len=64) at 200qps.
   - watch kv_cache.hit_rate, queue_depth, and per-request latency.
   - commands:
     - ./scripts/seed-workload --qps 200 --seq 64 --target staging-a1
     - kubectl logs -f pod/runtime -c runtime | grep "cache_miss_handler"
2) Inject NVLink-reset simulation (if staging supports):
   - echo 1 > /sys/bus/pci/devices/<dev>/reset (careful) OR use nvidia-smi --gpu-reset on test nodes.
   - measure behavior after reset under load.
3) Turn off aggressive compaction in config and re-run autoscale stress to see if p99 persists.

Instrumentation TODOs (short actionable):
- [ ] Add trace span around cache_miss_handler (owner: Reece) — short term add logs with correlation_id and kv_key. Ticket: INF-7140
- [ ] Emit metric for "cache_refill_latency_ms" (owner: Asha) — helps see refill cost distribution. Ticket: INF-7141
- [ ] Add guard in scheduler to cap instantaneous queue growth (owner: SRE) — proposal: soft-queue-limit that returns 503 earlier with retry-after header.
- [ ] Add health-check hook to influence autoscaler faster (owner: infra-team)

Notes on possible mitigations (quick wins):
- Backoff compaction during high qps windows (schedule compaction windows).
- Increase small-burst buffer in autoscaler to handle 5m spikes.
- Circuit-breaker: prefer fast fallback to smaller model variant instead of stalling (routing policy).

Open questions / unknowns:
- Are nvlink resets cause or effect? (Does compaction trigger some driver stress?)
- Why did autoscaler not react for 2m? (rate-limit on reserved capacity?)
- Did any recent kernel change land that could cause increased PCI bus activity? (PRs checked: none obvious but double-check PR 2887 net/pci tweaks)

Quick timeline to share with oncall and infra:
- 02:35 alert threshold crossed
- 02:38 nvlink resets logged
- 02:40 p99 spike peaked at +1.8s
- 02:42 eq: queue depth reduced after manual drain and queued requests timed out (some 503s generated)
- 02:47 normal levels restored

Owner actions for today:
- Reece: run staging repro + attach full trace dump to INF-7123 (ETA today EOD PT).
- Asha: add metric for refill latency (temp) and push tiny logging patch.
- SRE: check autoscaler logs and rate-limits for dedicated-nyc-1 pool.

Meeting sync notes (standup 10:30 PT):
- Bring a short summary and repro plan. Ask SRE about autoscaler cold-start config.
- Ask infra if we can simulate nvlink resets safely in staging.

Scratchpad ideas (thinking aloud):
- Could we tolerate a short lived model fallback (small/quantized variant) while recovery happens? That would reduce tail but risks quality regression. Maybe do canary with 10% traffic first.
- Consider a lightweight cache-occupancy probe that runs per-host and pre-warms KV for hot prefixes after compaction completes.

Relevant commands / snippets saved for runbook:
- kubectl port-forward svc/runtime-metrics 9090:9090
- curl -s localhost:9090/metrics | grep kv_cache
- ./scripts/profile-request --model tiny-q8 --seq 64 --log-trace > trace.out

Done for morning. Will update INF-7123 with trace dump and basic repro notes. Keep this doc as ephemeral scratch — convert to runbook if repro confirmed.

Reece
